Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing dizziness, nausea, and imbalance. To help me determine the cause, how long have these symptoms been occurring, and is the dizziness a spinning sensation or just feeling faint?

speaker: Doctor

REQUEST TEST: Audiometry

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Vestibular_Function_Test: Unstable tandem gait noted with reported sensation of imbalance; Positional testing (lying flat rapidly with head turned) does not provoke symptoms. Audiometry: Bilateral decreased hearing sensitivity noted, specific details not specified.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The vestibular function test shows an unstable tandem gait, and the audiometry reveals bilateral decreased hearing sensitivity. Since the positional testing did not provoke symptoms, do you have a history of sudden vertigo attacks or any recent head trauma, and do you experience tinnitus or ear fullness?

REQUEST IMAGES: MRI_Auditory_Brainstem

speaker: Patient
text: 27-year-old male. The patient reports a sustained sensation of the room spinning since this morning, which is low grade and constant. He occasionally feels nauseous and has taken diphenhydramine to help him sleep, which also alleviates his symptoms slightly. He mentions recent increased intake of garlic due to trying to recover from a cold a few days ago. Past medical history is unremarkable.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Acoustic Neuroma (Vestibular Schwannoma)

Your recent MRI of the auditory brainstem has returned, please wait a moment while I review the images to confirm the bilateral hearing loss and your specific symptoms.
